en.title: Breeze Airways adds six new destinations and picks up routes left by Spirit
en.summary: Breeze Airways will add services to six new destinations in the coming months, extending its point-to-point network between secondary airports and unserved markets, replacing Spirit on a number of routes and adding international destinations in Jamaica and the Dominican Republic.
body: Breeze Airways continues to develop its niche network of point-to-point flights between secondary airports or unserved markets. The Utah-based airline, another carrier developed by aviation entrepreneur David Neeleman, who also supported the establishment of Azul, JetBlue and WestJet, operates a fleet of 66 Airbus A220-300 aircraft. In the coming months it will add services to six new destinations, replacing Spirit on a number of routes while also adding new international destinations in Jamaica and the Dominican Republic.

As Spirit Airlines collapsed earlier this year, a number of popular leisure routes were left unserved, and Breeze has been one airline stepping up at Myrtle Beach International Airport, where it is now one of the largest carriers by destinations served. This coming February, Breeze will reconnect Myrtle Beach with Latrobe and Boston Logan International Airport with regular nonstop flights: Latrobe to Myrtle Beach starts February 9 with no other airline operating the route, Latrobe to Orlando starts May 26, and Myrtle Beach to Boston starts May 4, where American Airlines and Delta Air Lines also operate. The reintroduction of flights to Latrobe reestablishes commercial air service at the Pennsylvania airport that otherwise was left abandoned by Spirit. From Tampa, Breeze will add Montego Bay from December 19 and Santo Domingo from June 18, plus St. Thomas on December 16, which is not classed as an international flight and needs no passport. Buffalo Niagara International Airport will gain three new routes next June and July: to Myrtle Beach on July 1, to Raleigh on June 29, where Frontier Airlines maintains a seasonal service, and to Charleston on July 2, with no other airline operating the other two routes.

facts.claim: Breeze Airways will add services to six new destinations in the coming months, replacing Spirit on a number of routes and adding new international destinations in Jamaica and the Dominican Republic.
Breeze is a Utah-based airline developed by David Neeleman, who also supported the establishment of Azul, JetBlue and WestJet, and operates a fleet of 66 Airbus A220-300 aircraft.
Spirit Airlines collapsed earlier this year, leaving popular leisure routes unserved, and Breeze is now one of the largest carriers at Myrtle Beach by destinations served.

Latrobe to Myrtle Beach starts February 9 with no other airline operating the route, Latrobe to Orlando starts May 26, and Myrtle Beach to Boston starts May 4 with American Airlines and Delta Air Lines as competition.

Breeze will add Tampa to Montego Bay from December 19, Tampa to Santo Domingo from June 18, and Tampa to St. Thomas on December 16, which is not classed as an international flight and needs no passport.

Buffalo will gain three new Breeze routes: to Myrtle Beach on July 1, to Raleigh on June 29 with seasonal Frontier Airlines competition, and to Charleston on July 2, with no other airline operating the other two routes.

zh.title: 微風航空新增6個航點並接手精神航空遺留航線
zh.summary: 微風航空未來數月將新增6個航點，延續其連接次要機場與未開發市場的點對點網絡，接手部分精神航空退出後留下的航線，並新增牙買加與多明尼加航點。
body: 微風航空持續發展其連接次要機場或未開發市場的點對點利基網絡。這家猶他州航空公司由航空創業家大衛尼爾曼創辦，他也曾協助創立阿祖爾航空、捷藍航空與西捷航空，機隊擁有66架空中巴士A220-300。未來數月，微風航空將新增6個航點，在部分航線接手精神航空退出後的市場，同時新增牙買加與多明尼加國際航點。

精神航空今年稍早倒閉後，許多熱門休閒航線無人服務，微風航空是填補空缺的業者之一，如今已是默特爾比奇機場按航點數計最大的業者之一。今年2月起，微風航空將以定期直飛航班重新連接默特爾比奇與拉特羅布及波士頓洛根機場：拉特羅布往默特爾比奇2月9日開航且無其他業者競爭，拉特羅布往奧蘭多5月26日開航，默特爾比奇往波士頓5月4日開航，美國航空與達美航空也在該航線營運。重返拉特羅布讓這座賓州機場在精神航空退出後重新擁有商業航班。坦帕方面，微風航空將於12月19日開航蒙特哥貝、6月18日開航聖多明各，12月16日開航聖托馬斯，後者不屬於國際航班，旅客無需護照。水牛城尼加拉機場明年6月與7月也將新增3條航線：7月1日往默特爾比奇、6月29日往羅利、7月2日往查爾斯頓，其中羅利航線有邊疆航空季節性航班競爭，其餘兩條航線無其他業者營運。
